recipes.name: Rosemary and Garlic Simmered Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 4 (6 ounce) boneless center-cut pork loin chops, trimmed of fat

steps.text: Combine rosemary, ground pepper, and salt in a small bowl; rub rosemary mixture on pork chops.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat; stir garlic into melted butter, then place pork chops in the skillet. Cook until golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes per side.

Reduce heat to low and pour in beef broth. Simmer until pork chops are fully cooked, 35 to 45 minutes. A meat thermometer inserted into the center of the thickest chop should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Rosemary and Garlic Simmered Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: These easy and tasty garlic rosemary pork chops are cooked on the stove in minutes. Rosemary and beef broth enrich the flavor of the meat and make this a great comfort food main dish.

review.reviewBody: This would have been a 5, had I followed the recipe! I didn't have any beef stock, so I used beef bouillon with 1 cup of water. After reducing so much during the cooking, the sauce became so salty it was almost inedible! So... note to others, DO NOT USE BEEF BOUILLON!

I did it twice. First time was disappointing because spices were washed out while simmering. Second time I used the instant pot and kept the pork out of the broth. Also threw in some potatoes and carrots. Worked great!! Ten minutes in pressure 4 minutes release for one and a half pounds.

I used half white wine/half water instead of the beef stock and added some dried tarragon to the fresh rosemary I had on hand. It turned out pretty good, quite moist as well. I cooked it covered. Then removed the chops and reduced the liquid to make a pleasant sauce. I used minimal salt and pepper. I’m cooking for one person, me. I served it with steamed asparagus and mashed potatoes.

Family really liked this. Only changes I made was using 1/2 cup beef broth and 1/2 cup of Marsala wine as it was by my stove. Do not go by cooking time as stove temps are different. Cooked each side for 3 min and then used a meat thermometer until it got to 145 degrees F which only took 20 minutes to gauge the doneness. 35-45 minutes would have dried out the meat. The juice in the pan was great over the pork as well as a baked potato. dmoneil

I didnt have any beef broth handy so I winged it with a 1/4 cup worcestershire and 3/4 cup water mixture. Followed the rest of the recipe and it came out excellent! Adding this to the weekly dinner routine.

I needed a new pork chop recipe that was fast and easy but also something that my 9 year old son would eat. He is tired of me making the same meat recipes and decided to become a vegetarian. So when I agreed to look for new recipes he agreed to eat meat again.
Thank you so much for sharing this as he ate a whole butterfly pork chop. I did alter it a bit only because I did not have all the exact ingredients. I seasoned them with a little oregano, garlic and black pepper. I rubbed the pork with these 3 and browned them in EVOO. I then added a can of beef broth and simmered. Was absolutely wonderful! Very moist and broke apart with a fork. I will definitely add this one to my favorite recipes!

I made this last night and it was delicious! I used Emeril's beef stock instead of low sodium beef stock and it did not turn our too salty. I also added a splash of Chianti. I made basmati rice, cute the pork chops into cubes, and spooned the pork chops and au jus over the rice. My 4 year old twin girls even liked it! And so easy! This one is definitely in the weekly rotation.

These were GREAT! My fiance and I both loved them. I did make some changes. I had no rosemary, so I subbed italian herbs instead. I used beef bouillon, but as another reviewer said it was too salty this way, I skipped adding salt and also used 1 1/2 cups water to one bouillon cube. I also added a T of cornstarch at the end as suggested by other reviewers. Fabulous!

The flavor on this was amazing! I didn't have beef stock, so I used chicken. After I pulled the pork I made a quick gravy with some cornstarch and water. It was delicious. I will definately make this again.

This was delicious! I had 4 (thicker) boneless loin chops and trimmed all of the extra fat before cooking. The only thing I changed in this recipe is that I used Extra Virgin Olive Oil instead of butter. This is a new go-to dish. Really tasty and very simple to prepare. After adding the beef broth, I low-cooked the chops around 45-50 minutes and they were very tender. I served this with steamed snap peas and a small serving of (previously prepared) "chili rice pot". The chili rice pot dish contains a combination of 1 1/2-2 c. cooked brown rice, a can of organic tri-beans (pinto, black & kidney), a can of diced tomatoes (I used Hunt's Basil, Garlic & Oregano diced tomatoes) , 1 c. water, and a 1/2 teaspoon each of chili powder and garlic powder. This entire meal had a wonderful combination of complementary flavors.
Everyone here loves it. I substitute Italian seasoning for the rosemary and I use minced garlic with red pepper.
Made the recipe just as it said. We have a large family & it seemed to be one everyone liked! Definitely adding to my pork chop go to collection!
Mine turned out very dry
Thank you for sharing your recipe. It was very easy, and tasted good. I will be making this again.
Followed the recipe to a T, and the family was disappointed because they were dry. think we can reduce the cooking time next time, as the flavor was good.
Fantasy recipe!! I don’t even like most pork dishes but this one recipe has won me over.

We are garlic people, so I added 4 cloves of garlic. Always a fan of rosemary! Pork chops came out nice and juicy, they will be served with cauliflower rice and sautéed mushroom. Quick and easy dinner with ingredients that I always have on hand.
Next time I would def add less salt. I’m used to hardly any in my cooking and this was too salty for me. But the rest was good enough to try again
It was very good. No changes made.
Made it as written, turned out great!
